request: We should know which of our contacts are most influential so we can prioritize them.
pre_mortem: A year after launch, the influence scoring system led to a major diplomatic incident when a regional coordinator mistakenly prioritized outreach to a low-influence but politically sensitive contact, believing them to be high-influence based on outdated criteria. The contact, feeling neglected in favor of more senior representatives, leaked sensitive information which created international tensions and damaged relations with key stakeholders.
gaps: Which roles can see the influence scores and the criteria used for scoring?
What specific criteria will define 'global position,' and how can they vary per country or organization?
What happens to the influence scoring if the data becomes inaccurate or outdated, considering contacts can change roles frequently?
How will users provide feedback about the scoring system, and how will that feedback be incorporated into updates?
What safeguards are in place to ensure that influence scores won't be misinterpreted or misused by users?
How often will the scoring criteria be reviewed to ensure relevance and accuracy?

proposals.summary: This release delivers a contact influence scoring system to help prioritize outreach to influential contacts for regional coordinators and project managers. It will assess and display influence levels for contacts based on predefined criteria within the Government CRM system.

core_commitments.text: Enable users to view an influence score for each contact so they can prioritize engagement efforts.

in_scope.text: Establish an influence scoring system that assigns a score from 1 to 10 for each contact based on three criteria: global position, mission involvement, and historical engagement frequency.
Allow regional coordinators and project managers to filter and sort their contact list based on influence scores.
Display influence scores alongside existing contact information in the CRM for all user roles.
Provide an interface where users can view the criteria used to assess influence scores.

out_of_scope.text: This release will not include automated scoring updates; scores will be manually entered by designated users.
Social media influence or external metrics will not be included in the scoring system for this release.
Collaboration features or access controls beyond the basic CRM role permissions are out of scope for this release.

assumptions.text: Users will have sufficient permissions to view influence scores, depending on their role in the organization.
The scoring criteria will be agreed upon by stakeholders before implementation begins.
Influence scoring does not violate any data protection regulations concerning how contact information can be assessed or displayed.
Contact data will be up to date and accurate to ensure correct scoring.

definitions.text: 'Influence score' means a numerical value ranging from 1 (minimal influence) to 10 (maximum influence) assigned to each contact based on their role, involvement in missions, and historical engagement frequency.
'Global position' means the current job title or role of a contact within their respective organization that signifies their level of authority.
'Mission involvement' means the number of active projects or missions a contact is associated with within the CRM system.
'Historical engagement frequency' means the number of interactions recorded in the CRM between the organization and the contact over the past 12 months.

success_criteria.text: Achieve a minimum of 80% user satisfaction with the influence scoring feature as assessed by user feedback surveys within three months of deployment.
At least 70% of users utilize the influence score filtering and sorting feature at least once a month after release.
